summary: Completed comprehensive testing of multi-provider OAuth sign-in feature (Google, Apple, Microsoft, Facebook). All 14 backend tests passed. Frontend OAuth buttons verified on both Login page and Settings > Security section.

Google_OAuth_Callback.details: Creates new user if not exists, updates existing user, sets google_connected=true, returns valid JWT token

Apple_OAuth_Callback.details: Creates new user if not exists, updates existing user, sets apple_connected=true, returns valid JWT token

Microsoft_OAuth_Callback.details: Creates new user if not exists, updates existing user, sets microsoft_connected=true, returns valid JWT token

Facebook_OAuth_Callback.details: Creates new user if not exists, updates existing user, sets facebook_connected=true, returns valid JWT token

JWT_Token_Validation.details: OAuth callback returns valid JWT token that works for protected endpoints like /api/auth/me

Multi_Provider_Connection.details: User can connect multiple OAuth providers to same account (e.g., Google + Apple)

Input_Validation.details: Missing email returns 422, missing session_token returns 422

Login_Page_OAuth_Buttons.details: All 4 OAuth buttons visible: 'Continue with Google', 'Continue with Apple', 'Continue with Microsoft', 'Continue with Facebook'

Settings_Security_OAuth_Connect.details: Connected Accounts section shows all 4 providers (Google, Apple, Microsoft, Facebook) with Connect buttons and proper icons

seed_data_creation: OAuth test users created during backend testing with TEST_ prefix
context_for_next_testing_agent: Multi-provider OAuth fully implemented and tested. All 4 providers (Google, Apple, Microsoft, Facebook) work on both Login page and Settings > Security. Backend endpoints create/update users correctly and return valid JWT tokens. AuthCallback.js component handles OAuth redirects from all providers.
